public_headline: United Airlines Crew Reported Three Blinking Lights Over Nebraska in 2023
public_tldr: This FAA preliminary report documents a sighting by the crew of United Airlines flight 476 on 4 October 2023. While cruising at roughly 35,000 feet over western Nebraska, the crew observed three stationary bright white lights blinking in a sequential pattern off the left side of the aircraft. No evasive action was taken and no investigation results are included.
public_narrative:
This document is a preliminary information report from the FAA's Washington Operations Center. It records a UAP (unidentified aerial phenomenon) sighting reported by a commercial airline crew — not a completed investigation or any kind of conclusion about what was seen.

On 4 October 2023 at 03:25 MDT, the crew of United Airlines flight 476 — a Boeing 737-900 flying from San Francisco to Chicago O'Hare — spotted something unusual while at flight level 350, approximately 35,000 feet. The sighting occurred about 42 nautical miles northeast of Scottsbluff, Nebraska, at coordinates 42.3°N, 103.0°W. The crew described three stationary bright white lights blinking in a left-to-right and right-to-left pattern, visible from the left side of the aircraft.

The crew did not take evasive action, and no law enforcement was notified. The report was relayed through Denver ARTCC (Air Route Traffic Control Center) to FAA operations.

The document contains no follow-up analysis, no radar data, no photographs, and no determination of what the lights were. It is a single-page preliminary record — essentially a logbook entry that an unusual sighting was reported through official channels.
public_caveats: This is a preliminary report only — the FAA did not reach any conclusion about what the lights were.
The account comes from a single flight crew. No corroborating radar data, photographs, or independent witness reports are included in the document.
No follow-up investigation results appear in this record. It is unknown whether any further inquiry was conducted.

The location and flight details are consistent with the stated route, but some specifics (aircraft type, altitude, exact position) are inferred from abbreviated aviation shorthand rather than spelled out in full.
There is little evidence of redaction in this document — the limited detail reflects the nature of a preliminary report, not deliberate withholding.
